## Source versions

- [YouTube: Why Young Americans Feel Locked Out with the Lemonade Stand Podcast | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 82](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pTFWpojm1dU) - 2026-11-02
- [Substack: Why Young Americans Feel Locked Out with the Lemonade Stand Podcast](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/why-young-americans-feel-locked-out) - 2026-11-01

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman and Lemonade Stand hosts discuss entry-level jobs, housing affordability, AI concentration, automated cash management, leveraged software buyouts and insurance regulation. Eisman remains supportive of long-horizon S&P saving despite near-term risks. He overstates the impossibility of higher-level zoning reform and Schwab's dependence on cash spreads. Guest anecdotes are kept separate from Eisman's assertions; severe housing declines are attributed to Melody Wright rather than adopted as Eisman's target.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

### 008. There is zero probability of US state or federal authorities overriding local zoning to permit more housing.

## Framework and tools

- Separate housing consumption from expected investment gains.
- Trace AI effects into deposits and financial intermediation.
- Use residual-equity arithmetic, but state valuation assumptions.
- Keep long-horizon savings distinct from near-term cyclical risk.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Mortgage lock-in comparison
- S&P and bond AI exposure
- Schwab cash-sweep example
- PE leverage and redemption example
- Software buyout waterfall

## Source cautions

Eisman is identifiable by questions, first-person history and long analytical answers. The two Lemonade Stand guests are often not distinguishable from text alone, so their claims use Uncertain speaker rather than fabricated names.
- Guest turns are not consistently labeled; individual Aidan McCaig versus Brandon Ewing attribution is uncertain.
- The 30%-50% housing decline belongs to reported guest Melody Wright.
- Specific Mark Walter allegations require primary documentary corroboration.
